title: [SDK 50] Pod install error: The Swift pod `ExpoModulesCore` depends upon `glog`, which does not define modules
body: I have a minimal reproduction at https://github.com/NervJS/taro-native-shell/tree/0.73.0. During the build, pod installation exits with code 1 because the Swift pod `ExpoModulesCore` depends on `glog`, which does not define modules. The action log is https://github.com/NervJS/taro-native-shell/actions/runs/7194009870/job/19593603408.

symptoms_visible: My GitHub Actions build exits with code 1 during pod installation and says that the Swift pod `ExpoModulesCore` depends on `glog`, which does not define modules.
N0.label: N0 glog module error reported

symptoms_visible: I do not have `expo-modules-core` in my dependencies, and the pod installation error is still present on the original runner.
N1_x.label: N1_x direct-dependency theory rejected

symptoms_visible: The workflow using the macOS 12 runner fails during pod installation with the `ExpoModulesCore` and `glog` module error.
N2.label: N2 failing runner identified

symptoms_visible: The pod installation succeeds in the macOS 13 comparison run; the corresponding macOS 12 run fails with the `glog` module error.
N3.label: N3 runner comparison verifies workaround

symptoms_visible: With the workflow kept on `runs-on: macos-13`, pod installation completes successfully and the `ExpoModulesCore` and `glog` module error no longer appears.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved on macOS 13 runner

solution.intent: Remove `expo-modules-core` from direct dependencies, reinstall JavaScript dependencies, and reinstall pods because it should only be pulled transitively by `expo`.
solution.concrete_example: Delete `expo-modules-core` from package.json, run yarn again, and reinstall the pods.

edges.comment: Initial maintainer resolution in c0 was rejected by the reporter in c1: `expo-modules-core` was not a direct dependency, so there was nothing to remove.

question_patterns: Which macOS runner is used by the failing GitHub Actions job?
Can you check the workflow or failing tag and tell me whether it runs on macOS 12 or macOS 13?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The failing v0.73.0-5 job uses the macOS 12 runner. Here is its pod-install log: https://github.com/NervJS/taro-native-shell/actions/runs/7204271154/job/19625441734.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The failing job already uses macOS 13, and switching between macOS 12 and macOS 13 produces the same error.
The failing workflow uses another macOS 12 image with the same available Xcode version.

edges.comment: The reporter later supplied the failing tag and job. Mapping the runner image to its default Xcode version is engineer-side inference, not part of this raw answer.

question_patterns: Can you run the same workflow once on `macos-13` and report whether pod installation succeeds?
Please compare the job on macOS 12 and macOS 13 and share the raw result.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The v0.73.0-6 job on macOS 13 succeeds: https://github.com/NervJS/taro-native-shell/actions/runs/7206623790/job/19631822473.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The macOS 13 job fails with the same `ExpoModulesCore` and `glog` module error.
The same job succeeds on macOS 13 in a rerun with a different tag name.

question_patterns: Was changing the runner the only difference between the failing and successful tags?
Can you share the diff between the failed and successful workflow revisions?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. The only change was `runs-on: macos-13`. This is the diff: https://github.com/NervJS/taro-native-shell/compare/v0.73.0-5...v0.73.0-6.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The successful revision also changed the Expo and React Native versions, regenerated the lockfile, and edited the Podfile.
The successful job has a different tag description, but its workflow and dependencies are otherwise the same except for the runner.

edges.comment: This edge records the raw failed/successful job comparison from c15. The conclusion that the older Xcode toolchain triggers the glog module-map problem belongs to the final solution's engineer inference.

solution.intent: Keep the CI workflow on `macos-13` or another environment with Xcode 14.3 or newer, rather than treating `expo-modules-core` as an invalid direct dependency; verify pod installation on that environment before declaring the issue resolved.
solution.concrete_example: Change the workflow from `runs-on: macos-12` to `runs-on: macos-13`, rerun the same pod-install job, and keep the change only after confirming that the job completes. The relevant difference is the newer Xcode toolchain on the macOS 13 image.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied only the runner names, the failed and successful job logs, and the one-line workflow diff. Engineers inferred that macOS 12 used Xcode 14.2 while macOS 13 used Xcode 14.3.1 by default, and connected the failure to React Native's conditional `DEFINES_MODULE` logic in `glog.podspec` for older Xcode versions.

edges.comment: The reporter's resolved configuration was the permanent `runs-on: macos-13` workflow change. Later comments identified upgrading to Xcode 15 as the preferred equivalent and patching `DEFINES_MODULE` as a workaround for machines that cannot upgrade.

question_patterns: Is `expo-modules-core` listed directly in your package.json?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No, I don't have `expo-modules-core` in my dependencies.

question_patterns: Which runner does the failing workflow use?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The failing v0.73.0-5 workflow uses the macOS 12 runner.

question_patterns: Please rerun the workflow on `macos-13` and tell me whether pod installation succeeds.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It succeeds on macOS 13. The successful job is https://github.com/NervJS/taro-native-shell/actions/runs/7206623790/job/19631822473.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It still fails with the same error on macOS 13.

question_patterns: Was changing to `runs-on: macos-13` the only change in the successful revision?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, changing the runner to `runs-on: macos-13` was the only change.

solution.intent: Switch the GitHub Actions workflow to `macos-13` or an environment with Xcode 14.3 or newer and verify that the same pod-install job succeeds.
solution.concrete_example: Use `runs-on: macos-13`, rerun the same workflow, and retain the runner change after pod installation completes successfully.
solution.inference_hint: A correct first response can avoid the rejected direct-dependency diagnosis by checking the manifest and comparing runner environments. The Xcode-version and glog-podspec explanation is inferred from the raw runner comparison.

edges.comment: Shortcut copy of the real resolution from the opening state, required because the first maintainer move was the falsified direct-dependency resolution.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the root cause as an older Xcode toolchain environment triggering the missing-module behavior for React Native's `glog` pod when imported by the Swift `ExpoModulesCore` pod; the reporter's macOS 12 runner failed while macOS 13 succeeded.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the failed macOS 12 job, successful macOS 13 job, and the reporter's confirmation that changing `runs-on` was the only difference.
Must not prescribe removing `expo-modules-core` as the resolution for this reporter, because it was not a direct dependency.

The primary resolution must be to use `macos-13` or an equivalent environment with Xcode 14.3 or newer; editing `DEFINES_MODULE` may only be presented as a fallback workaround for an environment that cannot be upgraded, not as the reporter's verified fix.
Must ask the user to rerun pod installation on the updated environment and must not declare resolution until that run succeeds.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable React Native and Expo maintainer who can inspect package dependencies, edit a GitHub Actions runner, compare release tags, and share CI logs and repository diffs.
persona_hint.communication_style: Very concise and evidence-oriented; answers direct questions with short statements and links to the exact failed job, successful job, and diff.
